Based on reading [[credential-scoping]] and [[runtime-paths]], here's how these two architectural decisions relate:

**Both enforce centralized control at the Hub's startup phase.** Credential-scoping ensures the API key is injected only into child processes' environments at spawn, never held by the Hub itself. Runtime-paths ensures every file location the Hub needs is resolved exactly once at startup from a single configuration point, before any code tries to discover paths independently.

**Together, they create a single-point-of-coordination pattern**: the Hub's initialization phase becomes the exclusive place where (1) all paths are discovered and validated, and (2) all secrets are provisioned into child processes. Neither credentials nor paths scatter across the codebase; both flow from deliberate, auditable entry points.

**This shared structure strengthens both security and reliability**. By centralizing path resolution, the system can validate that required files (including the secrets file itself) actually exist before running. By centralizing credential injection tied to that same startup phase, the system ensures credentials are only available to processes that have actually resolved their necessary runtime paths and are ready to use them.

In essence, credential-scoping and runtime-paths are two facets of the same architectural principle: **centralize all critical decisions (secrets + file locations) at a single entry point, before agents run, rather than spreading those decisions across runtime code paths.**
